newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS- US T-bond volatilities firm, trade light.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS- US T-bond volatilities firm, trade light.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. Treasury bond options were firm in afternoon trading ahead of Senate testimony by Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan Thursday and key economic data Friday, traders said.
"You've got a lot of things in the works, with Greenspan tomorrow and GDP (gross domestic product) Friday," one trader at a brokerage firm said.
Greenspan is scheduled to testify before the Senate Finance Committee beginning at 0900 CST/1500 GMT Thursday. On Friday, fourth quarter U.S. gross domestic product data are due at 0730 CST/1330 GMT.
The trader added that next week's meeting of the Fed's policy-setting unit, the Federal Open Market Committee or FOMC, also kept volatilities well bid.
"Most people still expect nothing (out of the FOMC meeting Tuesday and Wednesday) but there will be some attention to it and it will keep a bid in volatilities," he said.

Implied volatility for CBOT March T-bond futures options was around 10.75 percent, little changed from Tuesday's closing. Volatility in the June contract was trading between 10.25 and 10.30 percent, after closing at about 10.25 percent Tuesday.
March T-bond futures were struggling to hang on to slim gains around 110-07/32 in afternoon trading after a choppy morning and Tuesday's wild swings.
Dealers said activity in Treasury futures options was moderate but that most of the large trades were not directional in nature.
They said the 1.7 percent drop in December U.S. durable goods orders, larger than expected, had little impact.
"It's been relatively low volume today," one Eurodollar trader said. "I think everyone's just going to hang back until Friday's numbers."
Traders said implied volatilities for June and September Eurodollar futures options were down slightly from Tuesday's levels, with June at about 11.70 percent and September at around 14.6 percent.

A few sizable trades were seen, including the sale by a large U.S. brokerage house of around 4,000 of the June 9375 puts. An overseas bank was said to have sold the March 9425 put/March 9450 call strangle about 2,000 times.
Traders also cited a "short put tree" executed by a U.S. investment bank.
They said the firm bought the June 9350 puts and then sold the June 9325 and 9300 puts.
June Eurodollar futures were trading about flat at 94.22 in afternoon activity.
